text:
Maria: Pushed a profiling snapshot for the streaming+batches regression. Short summary: 95th latency up ~18% for L4 when streaming is on. Link: <https://internal/reports/2381234567>
Tom: Seen it. Flame shows an extra 4-7ms in the partial-decode queue path, seems correlated with smaller batch sizes.
Sasha: Logs uploaded and minimal repro script in the gist. Repro: loadgen streaming=true, batch_window_ms=6, token_budget_target=32.
Kevin: Key hypothesis: recent change lowered token_budget_target for interactive workloads. With streaming we hit that budget early, trigger an early flush + partial decode, which increases kernel switches and kernel-selection overhead.
Maria: Perf counters: kv_miss_rate jumped from 0.8% -> 3.4% under the repro. Also saw kernel_switches/request go from 0.9 -> 1.6.
Tom: That kv miss spike explains extra latency — small coalesced batches push KV cache eviction/warmup churn. Could try drain-before-flush or larger token budget.
Sasha: Quick experiment: set token_budget_target=64 on my dev rig and batch_window_ms=8. Result: kernel switches -22%, 95th down ~9%, but GPU mem high and more long-tail single-request prefetches.
Kevin: Idea: adaptive budget ramping. Start conservative for first 1-2 tokens, then ramp token_budget_target up over ~300-500ms if we detect frequent partial-decode handoffs. Pseudocode config: ```json
{"stream": {"token_budget_target": "auto", "budget_ramp_ms": 400}}
```
Maria: Add a metric `kernel_switches_per_request` + `partial_decode_handoffs` and an alert if kernel_switches_per_request > 1.2 for 1m.
Tom: Also try toggling kv prefetch hysteresis: if kv_miss_rate > 1% for 5s, raise prefetch_keepalive or pause evictions. That should reduce warmup churn.
Sasha: I'll run a canary on the dedicated pool with streaming enabled + the bumped budget config. Will report numbers later today.
ci-bot: deploy queued -> canary/dedicated/streaming-kv-ramp (owner: Sasha)
Kevin: I'll prototype the adaptive budget sampler in a small patch — it should be opt-in and behind a flag. Keep kernel-selection logging for a few hours to validate effect.
Maria: Also check that kernel-selection fallback path (small-kernel -> large-kernel) isn't triggered more because of quantized kernel thresholds. We might need a tiny hysteresis there.
Tom: Good call. I'll add kernel-selection hysteresis and a guard against switching within X ms of the last switch.
Sasha: Canary results (after 1h): kernel_switches/request dropped to 1.02 from 1.6, 95th latency improvement ~11%, kv_miss_rate stabilized ~1.1%. GPU mem up ~4%.
Maria: Nice. Sounds promising. Action items: Sasha run 24h canary, Tom add hysteresis & metric alert, Kevin land adaptive budget behind flag, Maria draft runbook note for streaming perf regressions. Assigned: Sasha/Tom/Kevin/Maria. :thumbsup:
Tom: I'll open PRs for the metrics + hysteresis today.
Maria: Thanks everyone. We'll regroup after 24h canary.
